'''Nirit Dudovich''' ({{Langx|he|'נירית דודוביץ}}) is an Israeli physicist who is the Robin Chemers Neustein Professorial Chair at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]. Her work considers strong field light–matter interactions and the generation of [[attosecond]] pulses. She was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2016.

== Early life and education ==
Dudovich was born in [[Jerusalem]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Chini|first=Michael|date=2020-02-27|title=Nirit Dudovich {{!}} ATTO VIII Conference|url=https://sciences.ucf.edu/physics/atto/person/nirit-dudovich/|access-date=2021-06-21|website=sciences.ucf.edu|language=en-us}}</ref> Her father Arnold Frank was a physicist.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=חלוץ |first=דינה |date=2021-12-26 |title=פרופ' נירית דודוביץ', זוכת פרס ויצמן למדעים מדויקים, סוגרת מעגל |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/laisha/article/bye3tc11ot |access-date=2025-05-04 |work=Ynet |language=he}}</ref> In 1989 she joined the [[Israel Defense Forces]] in the Intelligence Corps, where she served until 1993.<ref name=":0" /> She was an undergraduate student in physics and computer sciences at [[Tel Aviv University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Physics - Nirit Dudovich|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/nirit_dudovich|access-date=2021-06-21|website=physics.aps.org}}</ref><ref name="Nirit Dudovich">{{Cite web|title=Nirit Dudovich|url=https://iias.huji.ac.il/people/nirit-dudovich|access-date=2021-06-21|website=iias.huji.ac.il|language=en}}</ref> She moved to the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] as a graduate student, earning both a master's and graduate degree. Her research focused on quantum coherent control.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Dudovich|first=Nirit|title=Quantum coherent control with shaped femtoseconds pulses|date=2004|publisher=publisher not identified|location=Rehovot|language=English|oclc=884949988}}</ref> After graduating, Dudovich moved to the [[National Research Council Canada]].<ref name=":1" />

== Research and career ==
In 2007, Dudovich joined the faculty at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref name=":1" /> Her research considers strong-field light–matter interactions, with a particular focus on the dynamics at ultrafast timescales. To this end, Dudovich developed frequency-resolved optomolecular gating.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ferré|first1=A.|last2=Soifer|first2=H.|last3=Pedatzur|first3=O.|last4=Bourassin-Bouchet|first4=C.|last5=Bruner|first5=B. D.|last6=Canonge|first6=R.|last7=Catoire|first7=F.|last8=Descamps|first8=D.|last9=Fabre|first9=B.|last10=Mével|first10=E.|last11=Petit|first11=S.|date=2016-02-02|title=Two-Dimensional Frequency Resolved Optomolecular Gating of High-Order Harmonic Generation|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.053002|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=116|issue=5|article-number=053002|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.053002|pmid=26894708 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> She has considered two aspects of high harmonic generation, including ionisation and recombination. She has made use of [[attosecond]] physics to better understand electronic processes such as tunnelling.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=ליידי גלובס מציג: 50 המשפיעות 2019 - פרופ' נירית דודוביץ|url=https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001300539|access-date=2021-06-21|website=גלובס|language=he}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
* 2003 Chorafas Foundation Award for Outstanding Achievement and the Gad Resheff Memorial Prize for Outstanding Achievements in Research<ref name="Nirit Dudovich"/>
* 2004 Weizmann Institute Women in Science Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home {{!}} Women In Science|url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/WomenInScience/home|access-date=2021-06-21|website=www.weizmann.ac.il|language=en}}</ref>
* 2012 [[IUPAP Young Scientist Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=iupap|date=2021-02-03|title=AC1: Awards - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|url=https://iupap.org/who-we-are/internal-organization/affiliated-commissions/ac1-international-commission-for-optics/ac1-awards/|access-date=2021-06-21|language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2012 Israel Physics Society Prize for Young Physicist<ref>{{Cite web|title=The IPS Conference 2012 Prize {{!}} Israel Physical Society|url=http://www.israelphysicalsociety.org/ips-conference-2012-prize|access-date=2021-06-21|website=www.israelphysicalsociety.org}}</ref> 
* 2013 Krill Prize for Excellence in Scientific Research<ref>{{Cite web|title=Krill Prize|url=https://wolffund.org.il/the-krill-prize/|access-date=2021-06-21|website=Wolf Foundation|language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2015 Elected to the Israel Young Academy<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. Nirit Dudovich|url=http://www.young.academy.ac.il/Index2/Entry.aspx?nodeId=959&entryId=96|access-date=2021-06-21|website=www.young.academy.ac.il}}</ref>
* 2016 Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Elected as a Fellow of the American Physical Society|date=4 April 2016 |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/awards-and-appointments/prof-nirit-dudovich|access-date=2021-06-21}}</ref>
* 2017 Helen and Martin Kimmel Award for Innovative Investigation<ref>{{Cite web|title=Institute Prizes|url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/acadaff/awards-and-honors/institute-honors-and-prizes/Kimmel|access-date=2021-06-21|website=Academic Affairs Office|language=en}}</ref>
* 2019 Named one of the most influential women scientists in [[Israel]]<ref name=":2" />
* 2021 Weizmann prize for exact sciences<ref name=":3" />
